# APA — native Wall/Roof underside closure from PR59

The previous Trim specimen contacted a roof cutout perimeter. The existing SEO checker then treated a total shared area as an underside contact. This continuation uses the actual lower principal roof face and rejects top-face contact, retained operator holes, a physical gap, an unchanged Wall body and source-plane drift.

`prepare_roof_underside_specimen` reuses the accepted native Wall/Roof recipe, measured source dimensions, building materials and story. It selects a separate vacant position from the current model extents and produces the existing BIM Graph/SceneWriter plan. Two native creations and one `SubtractionUpwards` SEO operation suffice; no new Morph, Trim, executor or geometry engine is introduced. Shapely compares actual planar BREP contours through the shared face reader. Source bodies are rechecked by SceneWriter for core and adapter writes.

The native test produced real Wall/Roof underside contact **2.33623338255613 m²**, versus the source-derived expected **2.336233382576165 m²**. Actual Wall vertices remain below the pinned lower plane; native pair and surrounding architecture collision queries are empty. Material GUIDs, story and native types match the input. Save/Open and independent readback preserve **109 GUID /45 shared context records**, including all **107 accepted GUID/body/material/story signatures**. The earlier perimeter specimen, Beam pair and Ø200 terminal connection remain intact.

The request included `skipPolygonHoles=true`; native relation readback reports it false. That discrepancy remains **NOT_VERIFIED_REQUEST_READBACK_DIFFERENCE**. Actual geometry and the SEO relationship are independently proven. The initial strict flag verification failure is retained in the journal, followed by read-only reconciliation; the native write was never repeated. No assertion that the flag was applied is made. The installed query also ignores the SDK return code for its flag read, so the cause cannot be established without a separately approved provider diagnostic.

The user explicitly authorized the renamed saved isolated test copy. Its exact identity and saved-file hash were bound locally, and all107 accepted signatures matched before any write. Full private paths, original PLN/IFC files and raw dumps remain local. The narrow `bind_authorized_saved_copy` entry point does not enable arbitrary CLI project overrides.

All four original upper Wall/Roof gaps are measured from actual face overlap and the sloped lower plane, rather than a bounding-box distance. They remain unchanged because this pass preserves accepted elements. The working separate native scenario does not approve a full construction family, bearing capacity, fastening system or manufacturer assembly.

MEP remains BLOCKED for the circular/rectangular main-network bridge. The exposed `CreateMEPElements` offers only default Terminal/Accessory/Equipment/Fitting placement, without specified port sections. Installed routing placement passes empty rectangular/circular per-segment maps. The native SDK does support those maps, but the installed command does not expose them; `TransitionDefault` itself provides non-geometric settings rather than standalone sized placement. A future separately authorized provider extension could expose the existing route-local segment maps and qualify a transition with actual two-port readback. A GUID-preserving main-network connection remains a separate acceptance requirement. No global preferences, installed APX or existing routes were changed.

Actual IFC export: **52 elements,45/45 world bounds,26 material assignments,12 port relations,6 opening hosts and20 quantity matches/0 mismatches**. New `IfcWall` and `IfcRoof` match actual native BREP quantities and materials. SEO/contact relationship export semantics and full receiver compatibility remain NOT_VERIFIED.
